# Exporting Amazon Inspector Findings Reports

A findings report is a CSV or JSON file that provides a detailed snapshot of findings. It can be exported to AWS Security Hub CSPM, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon S3. Findings for resources in connected cloud providers, including Azure and GCP, can be exported as well.

## What a report contains

By default, a findings report includes data for all active findings. Without filter criteria, the report includes all Active findings in the current Region. If you are the delegated administrator for an organization, the report includes data for all member accounts in the organization. You can customize a report by creating and applying a filter.

The format you choose affects the fields included. The JSON option includes all fields for each finding, while the CSV option includes only a subset of about 45 fields.

The CreateFindingsReport API also exports only active findings by default. If you specify SUPPRESSED or CLOSED in the filter criteria, you can view suppressed or closed findings in an API-exported report.

## How export works

When exporting, Amazon Inspector encrypts findings data with an AWS KMS key that you specify, and stores the findings report in an Amazon S3 bucket that you specify. The KMS key must be in the same AWS Region as the S3 bucket. The S3 bucket must be in the same AWS Region as the findings data you want to export.

Only one findings report can be exported at a time. If an export is currently in progress, you can export another findings report only once it finishes.

## Permissions

To retrieve findings data and export it in reports, you must be allowed to perform inspector2:ListFindings and inspector2:CreateFindingsReport.

When you export a report for the first time, steps 1-3 are optional. If you use the Inspector console to export a report, you also need the following permissions:

- kms:GetKeyPolicy and kms:PutKeyPolicy.
- kms:DescribeKey and kms:ListAliases.
- s3:ListAllMyBuckets and s3:GetBucketLocation.
- kms:CreateKey, if you create a new KMS key.

## Configuring the KMS key and S3 bucket

The KMS key must be a customer managed, symmetric encryption key (SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT). Its key policy must give Amazon Inspector permission to use the key, so that Amazon Inspector can encrypt and export the report. The S3 bucket policy must allow Amazon Inspector to add objects to the bucket. If the bucket is owned by another account, the bucket owner must update the bucket policy.

The policies can use the following conditions:

- The aws:SourceAccount condition limits Amazon Inspector to adding reports only for the specified account.
- The aws:SourceArn condition limits Amazon Inspector to adding only findings reports created by the specified account and Region.

Together, the SourceAccount and SourceArn conditions help prevent the confused deputy problem. If you manually enable Inspector in a Region, add the Region code to the Service principal.

## Troubleshooting

**Timeouts.** Report generation times out if it takes longer than 12 hours. Adding filter criteria reduces the number of findings, and you can then retry the export.

**"Cannot have multiple reports in-progress."** If a report is already being generated for the account, creating another report yields this error. GetFindingsReportStatus returns the report ID of the report currently being generated, and CancelFindingsReport cancels an in-progress export using that report ID.

# Exporting Amazon Inspector findings reports

## Before you begin

Complete these prerequisites before any step that needs them.

- **IAM permissions** for the Inspector, KMS, and S3 actions needed to export reports and configure resources: inspector2:ListFindings, inspector2:CreateFindingsReport, kms:GetKeyPolicy, kms:PutKeyPolicy, kms:DescribeKey, kms:ListAliases, s3:CreateBucket, s3:PutBucketPolicy, s3:ListAllMyBuckets, s3:GetBucketLocation, and so on. If you will create a new KMS key, you also need kms:CreateKey.
- **An S3 bucket** in the same AWS Region as the findings data to export. Use an existing bucket or create a new one before proceeding. It stores the report.
- **An S3 bucket policy statement** that allows the Amazon Inspector service principal to add objects (s3:PutObject) to the bucket. The steps are on this page.
- **A customer managed, symmetric encryption AWS KMS key** (SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT) in the same Region as the S3 bucket. Use an existing key or create a new one. The steps for creating a key are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/create-keys.html.
- **A KMS key policy statement** that allows Amazon Inspector to use the key to encrypt the report. The steps are on this page.

## About findings reports

A findings report is a CSV or JSON file that provides a detailed snapshot of findings. You can export a report to AWS Security Hub CSPM, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon S3. Findings for resources in connected cloud providers, including Azure and GCP, can be exported.

By default, a findings report includes data for all active findings. Without filter criteria, the report includes all Active findings in the current Region. To customize a report, create and apply a filter. If you are the delegated administrator for an organization, the report includes data for all member accounts in the organization.

The JSON option includes all fields for each finding. The CSV option includes only a subset of about 45 fields.

## Permissions

The kms:CreateKey permission is needed only if you create a new KMS key. Being allowed to perform inspector2:ListFindings and inspector2:CreateFindingsReport is enough for you to retrieve findings data and export it in reports. The kms:GetKeyPolicy and kms:PutKeyPolicy permissions let you read and update the key policy. The kms:DescribeKey and kms:ListAliases permissions let you look up keys. The s3:ListAllMyBuckets and s3:GetBucketLocation permissions let you list buckets and find their Regions.

## Configure the S3 bucket and KMS key

When exporting, Amazon Inspector stores the findings report in a user-specified Amazon S3 bucket and encrypts the findings data with a user-specified AWS KMS key. The S3 bucket must be in the same AWS Region as the findings data to export. If the bucket is owned by another account, the bucket owner must update the bucket policy.

Encryption with your KMS key works only when all of the following hold: the KMS key is in the same AWS Region as the S3 bucket, the KMS key policy allows Amazon Inspector to use the key, and the S3 bucket policy allows Amazon Inspector to add objects to the bucket. The key must be a customer managed, symmetric encryption key (SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT).

Amazon Inspector can encrypt and export the report only if the key policy gives it permission to use the key.

In the policies, you can use the aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions. The aws:SourceAccount condition limits Amazon Inspector to adding reports only for the specified account. The aws:SourceArn condition limits it to adding only findings reports created by the specified account and Region. Together, the two conditions help prevent the confused deputy problem.

If you manually enabled Inspector in a Region, add the Region code to the Service principal.

## Export a report

You use the Inspector console to export a report. After you export a findings report for the first time, steps 1-3 are optional.

Only one findings report can be exported at a time. While an export is in progress, you cannot export another findings report; you can export another one only when none is in progress. If a report is already being generated for the account, creating another report yields the error "Cannot have multiple reports in-progress". GetFindingsReportStatus returns the report ID of the report currently being generated. CancelFindingsReport cancels an in-progress export using that report ID.

## Include suppressed or closed findings

The CreateFindingsReport API exports only active findings by default. You can view suppressed or closed findings in an API-exported report only when the API's default of active findings applies and you specify SUPPRESSED or CLOSED in the filter criteria.

## Timeouts

Report generation times out if it takes longer than 12 hours. When that happens, add filter criteria to reduce the number of findings, then retry the export.

regen_doc:
# Exporting Amazon Inspector Findings Reports

A findings report is a CSV or JSON file that provides a detailed snapshot of findings. A report can be exported to AWS Security Hub CSPM, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon S3. Findings for resources in connected cloud providers, including Azure and GCP, can be exported as well.

## Scope and filtering

By default, a findings report includes data for all active findings. If you are the delegated administrator for an organization, the report includes data for all member accounts in the organization. To customize a report, create and apply a filter. Without filter criteria, the report includes all Active findings in the current Region.

The CreateFindingsReport API likewise exports only active findings by default. If SUPPRESSED or CLOSED is specified in the filter criteria, you can view suppressed or closed findings in an API-exported report.

## Report formats

The JSON option includes all fields for each finding, whereas the CSV option includes only a subset of about 45 fields.

## Encryption and storage

When exporting, Amazon Inspector encrypts findings data with an AWS KMS key that you specify, and it stores the findings report in an Amazon S3 bucket that you specify. The following requirements apply:

- The S3 bucket must be in the same AWS Region as the findings data to export.
- The KMS key must be in the same AWS Region as the S3 bucket.
- The KMS key must be a customer managed, symmetric encryption key (SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT).
- The KMS key policy must allow Amazon Inspector to use the key, so that Amazon Inspector can encrypt and export the report.
- The S3 bucket policy must allow Amazon Inspector to add objects to the bucket. If the bucket is owned by another account, the bucket owner must update the bucket policy.

The policy can include the aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions. The aws:SourceAccount condition limits Amazon Inspector to adding reports only for the specified account. The aws:SourceArn condition limits Amazon Inspector to adding only findings reports created by the specified account and Region. Together, these conditions help prevent the confused deputy problem. If you manually enabled Inspector in a Region, add the Region code to the Service principal.

## Required permissions

If you use the Inspector console to export a report, you must be allowed to perform the following actions:

- inspector2:ListFindings and inspector2:CreateFindingsReport, so that you can retrieve findings data and export it in reports.
- kms:GetKeyPolicy and kms:PutKeyPolicy.
- kms:DescribeKey and kms:ListAliases.
- s3:ListAllMyBuckets and s3:GetBucketLocation.
- kms:CreateKey, if you create a new KMS key.

Steps 1-3 are optional once a findings report has been exported for the first time.

## Limits and troubleshooting

Only one findings report can be exported at a time. If an export is currently in progress, you must wait for it to finish before another findings report can be exported. If a report is already being generated for the account, creating another report yields the error "Cannot have multiple reports in-progress". In that case, GetFindingsReportStatus returns the report ID of the report currently being generated, and CancelFindingsReport cancels the in-progress export using that report ID.

Report generation times out if it takes longer than 12 hours. If that happens, add filter criteria to reduce the number of findings, and then retry the export.

# Exporting Amazon Inspector findings reports

A findings report is a CSV or JSON file that provides a detailed snapshot of findings. A findings report can be exported to AWS Security Hub CSPM, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon S3.

## Before you begin

Complete the following prerequisites before you export a report.

- **IAM permissions for Amazon Inspector, KMS, and S3 actions.** You need permissions to export reports and to configure the bucket and key. The steps are on this page.
- **An S3 bucket in the same Region as the findings data.** The bucket stores the report. You can use an existing bucket or create a new one.
- **An S3 bucket policy statement.** The statement must allow the Amazon Inspector service principal to put objects into the bucket. The steps are on this page.
- **A customer managed symmetric encryption KMS key in the same Region as the S3 bucket.** You can use an existing key or create a new one. The steps are at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/create-keys.html.
- **A KMS key policy statement.** The statement must allow Amazon Inspector to use the key to encrypt reports. The steps are on this page.

## What a report contains

By default, a findings report includes data for all active findings. If you are the delegated administrator for an organization, the report includes data for all member accounts in the organization. You can customize a report by creating and applying a filter. Findings for resources in connected cloud providers, including Azure and GCP, can be exported.

Without filter criteria, the report includes all Active findings in the current Region. The JSON option includes all fields for each finding. The CSV option includes only a subset of about 45 fields.

## Permissions

Your IAM identity needs the following permissions.

- To retrieve findings data and export it in reports, you must be allowed to perform inspector2:ListFindings and inspector2:CreateFindingsReport. Being allowed both is enough to retrieve findings data and export it in reports.
- To configure the key policy, you must be allowed to perform kms:GetKeyPolicy and kms:PutKeyPolicy.
- To select a key, you must be allowed to perform kms:DescribeKey and kms:ListAliases.
- To create a new KMS key, you must be allowed to perform kms:CreateKey. This applies only when you create a new KMS key.
- To select a bucket, you must be allowed to perform s3:ListAllMyBuckets and s3:GetBucketLocation.

## Configure the S3 bucket and KMS key

Amazon Inspector stores the findings report in a user-specified Amazon S3 bucket. The bucket must be in the same AWS Region as the findings data to export. If the bucket is owned by another account, the bucket owner must update the bucket policy.

When exporting, Amazon Inspector encrypts findings data with a user-specified AWS KMS key. This works only when all of the following hold: the KMS key is in the same AWS Region as the S3 bucket, the KMS key policy allows Amazon Inspector to use the key, and the S3 bucket policy allows Amazon Inspector to add objects to the bucket. The KMS key must be a customer managed, symmetric encryption key (SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT). Amazon Inspector can encrypt and export the report only when the key policy gives it permission to use the key.

In the policies, the aws:SourceAccount condition limits Amazon Inspector to adding reports only for the specified account. The aws:SourceArn condition limits Amazon Inspector to adding only findings reports created by the specified account and Region. Together, the SourceAccount and SourceArn conditions help prevent the confused deputy problem. If you manually enable Inspector in a Region, add the Region code to the Service principal.

## Export a report

You use the Inspector console to export a report. Steps 1-3 are optional. Once you have exported a findings report for the first time, that is enough to make steps 1-3 optional.

Only one findings report can be exported at a time. While an export is in progress, you cannot export another findings report. You can export another one only when no export is in progress.

## Suppressed and closed findings

The CreateFindingsReport API exports only active findings by default. You can view suppressed or closed findings in an API-exported report only when the API exports active findings by default and you specify SUPPRESSED or CLOSED in the filter criteria.

## Troubleshooting

**Timeouts.** Report generation times out if it takes longer than 12 hours. A timeout is enough to justify retrying: adding filter criteria reduces the number of findings, and the export can be retried.

**Multiple reports.** If a report is already being generated for the account, creating another report yields the error "Cannot have multiple reports in-progress". GetFindingsReportStatus returns the report ID of the report currently being generated. CancelFindingsReport cancels an in-progress export using that report ID.
